correctness.rationale: Every forward formula of depth \(d\) sees only \(d+1\) successor truth values, by structural induction; all positive syntax constructors are monotone on this prefix. The displayed lcm-exponent disjunctive normal form has the claimed truth on every permitted cycle and the CRT congruence witnesses rule out smaller positive depth. The Fine-Wilf periodic-prefix theorem establishes the Boolean upper bound; explicit cycles of lengths \(n\) and \(n-1\) disagree on past while agreeing on the entire shorter observable prefix. Boundary \(n=1\) and \(n=2\) are handled. Standard-library verify.py checks 127 length-set instances and 5,828 valuations (counted with repetitions), including both strict lower thresholds; these experiments are supporting, not proofs.

value.rationale: Uniform elimination of backward-time modality on a natural and widely studied restricted semantic class is a genuine expressive-power problem. The exact least depth contrasts linear Boolean and quadratic negation-free resources, and the arbitrary finite period-set lcm formula classifies a natural parameter family rather than an arbitrary numerical slice. The boundaries are tight in every case and the result supplies explicit syntax and matching countermodels; no downstream theorem or formula-size claim is assumed.
